summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her sixth cycle of high-dose methotrexate for primary colonic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. The chemotherapy was administered at a reduced dose of 3500 mg/m² and was well tolerated without mucositis. Leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, becoming undetectable by the third day. She received IVIG for common variable immune deficiency and pentamidine for PJP prophylaxis, though she experienced transient shortness of breath after pentamidine that resolved with albuterol. A concurrent C. difficile infection was diagnosed and treated with oral vancomycin. Her diabetes was managed by holding metformin during admission, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and close follow-up. She remained stable throughout the stay and was discharged in good condition.
